name: Isolated Geographic Pattern Capillary Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Geographic Pattern Capillary Malformation

criteria.description: Presence of a well-demarcated, geographic-shaped erythematous patch consistent with capillary malformation
No evidence of underlying venous or lymphatic malformations on imaging
Capillary malformation confined to skin without associated syndromic features
Lesion present at birth or within the neonatal period
Lesion remains stable in size and morphology without progressive hypertrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: distinct geographic pattern capillary malformation, absence of deep vascular involvement, and isolated skin involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by imaging to exclude deeper vascular anomalies.

pathognomonic.notes: Well-demarcated, flat, pink to red patch with irregular borders
Lesion present at birth or shortly thereafter

common.symptomName: Lesion color variation from pink to dark red
common.notes: Color intensity may vary with temperature or emotion
searchTerms: lesion color ranges pink to dark red
varied red shades in skin patch

common.notes: Typically does not thicken or develop nodularity

common.symptomName: Mild skin textural changes within lesion
common.notes: Slightly increased skin thickness or surface irregularity
searchTerms: slight skin texture changes in lesion

occasional.notes: Small visible dilated capillaries may be present
Increased sweating over the lesion area
Emotional distress related to visible lesion
Slight thinning of skin occasionally observed

rare.notes: Rare vascular proliferative lesion arising within malformation
searchTerms: growth of red, bleeding skin bump
secondary skin growth prone to bleeding

rare.notes: Fragility of capillaries may cause bleeding

imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing superficial capillary malformation without deep vascular anomalies
MRI to exclude associated venous or lymphatic malformations if clinically indicated
genetic: Somatic mutations in GNAQ gene reported in some capillary malformations but not routinely tested
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic geographic pattern lesion

distinguishingFeatures: Typically smaller, round or oval port-wine stains
Less commonly geographic or segmental pattern
May be associated with syndromic features

redFlags: Neurological symptoms such as seizures or developmental delay
Signs of deep vascular malformations or limb overgrowth
references: Happle R. Capillary malformations: clinical and molecular aspects. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2017.
Orphanet: Isolated geographic pattern capillary malformation. ORPHA:715345.
Happle R. Somatic mutations in GNAQ in capillary malformations. N Engl J Med. 2013.
